胡梅爾琴可能源自中世紀，當時以些微差異的變體遍及歐洲。十八世紀在荷蘭、法蘭德斯、: The hummel may date from the Middle Ages, when slightly differing versions were spread across Europe. In the eighteenth century it was common in the Netherlands, Flanders, northern Germany and Denmark; the earliest evidence in Swedish folk culture is from the seventeenth century, and it was most widespread in the south. In the nineteenth century it was regarded as a rough farm instrument and its popularity fell. It appeared in Flanders in the seventeenth century, was a favourite of soldiers in the trenches of the First World War, peaked in the 1920s and 1930s, and fell silent again after the 1930s. It was mainly a household instrument, widely played by women; after the folk revival of the 1970s enthusiasts took it up again.
胡梅爾琴平放於桌面，借助桌面共鳴放大聲音。旋律弦以手指或撥片向下撥奏；同調旋律弦: The hummel is laid flat on a table, and the table's resonance amplifies the sound. The melody strings are plucked downwards with the fingers or a pick; melody strings tuned in pairs are often stopped at the unison or a major third, and with an octave string this gives sixths. The accompaniment strings are mostly tuned to an open chord and are often strummed along with the melody. A beginner should first steady the body and tune the melody and accompaniment strings, then practise plucking downwards and stopping the frets.
胡梅爾琴是一種古老的鍵盤撥弦樂器，音色明亮而清脆，帶有獨特的金屬質感。其高音區尤: The hummel is an old keyed plucked instrument with a bright, crisp timbre and a distinctive metallic quality. Its treble is especially brilliant and clear, with a lightness like the harp's, while the middle and low registers are warm and round. The instrument sounds by plucking the strings with a mechanism, and its way of resonating is particular: it is neither as heavy as the piano nor as soft as the harpsichord, but closer to a blend of harp and harpsichord. Because the strings decay naturally, each note has a short sustain, and the sound is layered enough to carry easily through other instruments. Its range is moderate, and its timbre has both the elegance of old music and the clarity of a modern instrument, so that it shows its particular charm in chamber music and in solo playing.
胡梅爾琴是北歐舊式弦鳴樂器，與挪威長琴（langeleik）同類，近似早期齊特琴: The hummel is an old Nordic chordophone of the same kind as the Norwegian langeleik and close to the early zither. Its body is flat on top and bottom, thin-walled and pierced with a soundhole; it has few melody strings and many accompaniment strings, with about seventeen frets under the melody strings. It is laid flat on a table and plucked downwards with the fingers or a pick, and the accompaniment strings are usually tuned to an open chord. It was found in the folk music of the Netherlands, Flanders, northern Germany, Denmark and Sweden, was also a household instrument mostly played by women, and was used by Flemish soldiers in the First World War.
胡梅爾琴的共鳴箱主要採用雲杉、楓木等優質木材製作，以增強共鳴效果。琴弦通常採用鋼: The soundbox of the hummel is made mainly of good woods such as spruce and maple, to strengthen the resonance. The strings are usually steel or gut. The mechanical plucking action consists of precise metal gears and plectra, which keep the timbre accurate and even. The frame of the body is of hardwood for structural stability. Decorative parts may use ivory, bone or metal inlay, reflecting its standing as a fine instrument.
胡梅爾琴的實際演奏場合主要見於北歐與西北歐民間音樂，尤其瑞典南部、丹麥、北德、荷: The hummel was played mainly in the folk music of the Nordic and north-west European countries, especially southern Sweden, Denmark, northern Germany, the Netherlands and Flanders. The source names no particular composers or pieces, but shows that it was widely played at home by women, that it was popular among soldiers in the trenches of the First World War, and that enthusiasts took it up again in the folk revival of the later twentieth century. It is played lying flat on a table, plucked downwards with the fingers or a pick, and the melody and accompaniment strings often sound together.
